summary: After a plant closed, workers moved or commuted for years to other plants to reach a pension, and children were raised by relatives in the week.
realLife: Janesville, Wisconsin's GM plant ended production in December 2008. Hundreds of workers moved to plants elsewhere to keep jobs and reach pensions, and others stayed and commuted for years. One worker drove about eight hours each way at a cost the story put at as much as $6,000 a year. Families were split: a parent guided a teenager by phone while grandparents and a friend stayed with him on weeknights. New jobs in town generally paid less, and some workers changed careers.
sources: https://www.wpr.org/economy/gm-workers-reflect-life-10-years-after-janesville-plant-closure (Wisconsin Public Radio on GM workers ten years after the Janesville closure)
